Big Enough to Explore. Small Enough to Be Known.
Build your expertise in a department where research opportunities are broad, faculty mentorship is personal and your work can make a real impact.
With graduate programs spanning chemistry, biochemistry and physics, the department offers a collaborative research community connected to partners such as NASA and Sanford Research — giving you the opportunity to grow as an independent scientist while working closely with faculty.
Chemistry (M.S.)
From cancer-fighting compounds to ecofriendly manufacturing, SDSU’s chemistry research tackles real-world challenges through innovation and discovery. Our programs span environmental and bioanalytical chemistry, chemical sensor development, organic synthesis and more. Current projects explore drug discovery, climate change chemistry, advanced materials and cutting-edge analytical techniques.
From Molecules to Solutions: Chemistry in Action
Chemistry (M.S.) – Chemistry Education Specialization
Empower your students by deepening your understanding of chemistry. Designed for licensed, in-service science teachers, this flexible master's program blends online coursework with hands-on summer research at SDSU. Over two consecutive summers, you’ll enhance your chemistry expertise and bring richer, more effective learning into your classroom, all with minimal disruption to your teaching schedule.
Inspire Through Chemistry Education
Chemistry (Ph.D.)
From plant-derived cancer treatments to sustainable manufacturing solutions, SDSU’s chemistry research tackles challenges through creativity and scientific rigor. Our faculty and students explore a wide range of focus areas, including environmental chemistry, bioanalytical methods, chemical sensors, organic synthesis and materials development. Current projects span drug discovery, metabolomics, climate chemistry and advanced analytical techniques, grounded in the core disciplines of analytical, inorganic, organic and physical chemistry.
Innovate Solutions Through Chemistry Research
Biochemistry (M.S.)
An M.S. in biochemistry is a high-impact research degree designed to bridge the gap between foundational science and medical breakthroughs. Students lead cutting-edge projects in proteomics and cellular biochemistry within our state-of-the-art Avera Health and Science Center.
Master Molecular Breakthroughs
Biochemistry (Ph.D.)
At SDSU, biochemistry research investigates the molecular basis of life and disease, encompassing topics such as cancer, aging, immune function and protein interactions. Students work on cutting-edge projects, in areas such as structural biology, proteomics and cellular biochemistry, with opportunities to collaborate with Sanford Research to translate discoveries into real-world treatments.
Decode Life at the Molecular Level
Physics (M.S.)
From nuclear science and advanced materials to quantum technologies and the fundamental particles that make matter, SDSU’s physics M.S. program gives you the opportunity to explore how physics can shape the future. Build a strong foundation through advanced coursework and hands-on research while developing skills in experimentation, problem-solving and scientific analysis. Prepare for careers in research, technology, energy, healthcare, education and other growing fields — or take the next step toward a Ph.D.
Explore the Frontiers of Physics
Physics (Ph.D.)
Push the boundaries of physics through advanced training and original research at SDSU. Explore exciting questions across nuclear science, magnetic materials, quantum and energy technologies, fundamental particles and the forces that govern them, and more while working closely with faculty mentors. Gain the expertise to develop new knowledge, tackle complex scientific challenges and prepare for impactful careers in academia, national laboratories, industry and beyond.
Discover. Innovate. Advance Physics.
Frequently Asked Questions
What research opportunities are available?
Graduate students have opportunities to engage in research across chemistry, biochemistry and physics. Students work alongside faculty mentors on research that addresses real scientific questions. For more detail on the type of research opportunities in the department, please visit chemistry, biochemistry and physics research.
How do I find a faculty research mentor?
Students can explore faculty research interests to identify potential mentors whose work aligns with their academic and research goals. Graduate students work closely with faculty mentors as they develop their research expertise.

Biochemistry Research | South Dakota State University
Physics Research | South Dakota State University
When do graduate students begin research?
Graduate students have opportunities to become involved in research early in their program. Through hands-on research and close faculty mentorship, students develop the skills to investigate scientific questions and contribute to their field.
What is the difference between the M.S. and Ph.D. programs?
The M.S. combines advanced coursework with research experience and prepares students for careers in science and related fields, professional programs or further graduate study.
The Ph.D. emphasizes original research and prepares students to make independent contributions to their field and pursue research-intensive careers or industrial or academic careers that require more intensive training.
For more information on specific programs, please visit the specific program you're interested in:

Is financial support available for graduate students?
Graduate students may have opportunities for financial support through teaching assistantships, research assistantships, externally-funded fellowships and other funding opportunities.
Most graduate students in the department are guaranteed six semesters (two years) of teaching assistantship and have multiple opportunities for research assistantships. Research assistantships may be provided by the faculty research adviser through externally funded research projects. Funding and eligibility vary by program and funding source.
What academic background do I need to apply?
Applicants should have a strong academic background in chemistry, biochemistry, physics or a closely related field, depending on the program. Preparation in mathematics and relevant science coursework is important for success in graduate study.
For specifics, visit SDSU's academic catalog and degree finder.
What are the admission requirements and application materials?
Admission requirements vary by program and may include academic transcripts, letters of recommendation, a statement of purpose and other program-specific materials. Applicants should review the requirements for their intended program before applying.
For specifics on SDSU’s admissions requirements, visit graduate admissions and admission information.
Are there additional requirements for international students?
International applicants may have additional requirements, including proof of English-language proficiency, unless they qualify for an approved exemption or waiver. Applicants should review SDSU’s current international graduate admission requirements for details.
